english_explanations: the branch of topology that studies mathematical knots and how to tell them apart

chinese_translations.english: the branch of topology that studies closed loops of string and how to distinguish different knots
chinese_translations.example: Knot theory was born when pure mathematicians took over the study of knots from the physicists.

english_explanations: a closed loop of string embedded in three-dimensional space, with no free ends

chinese_translations.english: a closed loop in space that cannot be untied without cutting
chinese_translations.example: Mathematically, your shoelaces are only a knot if the ends are fused together into a closed loop.

english_explanations: a curve with no free ends, forming a complete circle-like path

chinese_translations.english: a path with no free ends, formed by fusing the ends of a string together
chinese_translations.example: Your laces are only a mathematical knot if they form a closed loop.

english_explanations: the branch of mathematics that studies properties preserved under continuous deformation

chinese_translations.english: the study of properties that stay the same when shapes are stretched or bent, but not cut
chinese_translations.example: Knot theory is a branch of topology.

english_explanations: a smooth deformation of the whole surrounding space that moves one knot onto another without cutting or passing strands through each other

chinese_translations.english: a smooth deformation of the surrounding space that carries one knot to another without cutting
chinese_translations.example: Two knots are equivalent exactly when an ambient isotopy carries one to the other.

english_explanations: the simplest nontrivial knot, with exactly three crossings

chinese_translations.english: the simplest knot that cannot be untied, shaped like a clover with three crossings
chinese_translations.example: The trefoil knot is tricolourable, but the figure of eight knot is not, so they are different knots.

english_explanations: a knot with four crossings whose diagram looks like the numeral 8

chinese_translations.english: a four-crossing knot that looks like the numeral 8
chinese_translations.example: Unlike the trefoil, the figure of eight knot cannot be tricoloured.

chinese_translations.english: a four-crossing knot that looks like the numeral 8
chinese_translations.example: Unlike the trefoil, the figure of eight knot cannot be tricoloured.

english_explanations: a simple closed loop with no knot in it, equivalent to an ordinary circle of string

chinese_translations.english: the simplest knot of all: an untangled closed loop, also called the trivial knot
chinese_translations.example: However tangled it looks, the diagram in Figure 3 unravels into the unknot.

english_explanations: a section of a knot diagram where the string is twisted and crossed in a complicated way

chinese_translations.english: a twisted, crossed section of string within a knot diagram
chinese_translations.example: Is the unknot equivalent to the tangle on the right? Knot so easy this time.

english_explanations: a two-dimensional drawing of a knot showing, at each crossing, which strand passes over

chinese_translations.english: a plane drawing of a knot in which breaks mark which strand passes under at each crossing
chinese_translations.example: From a knot diagram we can build the knot matrix and compute the Alexander polynomial.

english_explanations: the three basic ways of redrawing a knot diagram — a twist, a poke and a slide — none of which changes the knot

chinese_translations.english: the three basic diagram changes (twist, poke, slide) that never change the knot itself
chinese_translations.example: No sequence of Reidemeister moves can turn the trefoil knot into the figure of eight knot.

english_explanations: one continuous piece of the string in a knot diagram, running between crossings

chinese_translations.english: a continuous section of the string in a knot diagram
chinese_translations.example: Every strand of the knot diagram must be filled with one of the three colours.

english_explanations: a point in a knot diagram where one strand passes over another

chinese_translations.english: a point of the diagram where one strand of the knot passes over another
chinese_translations.example: Each crossing is labelled and becomes a row heading of the knot matrix.

english_explanations: the strand that passes on top at a crossing

chinese_translations.english: the strand that passes over the others at a crossing
chinese_translations.example: At each crossing, the overcrossing strand contributes a 2 to the knot matrix.

english_explanations: a strand that passes beneath another at a crossing

chinese_translations.english: a strand that passes under the others at a crossing
chinese_translations.example: The two undercrossing strands each contribute a -1 to the row of the matrix.

english_explanations: whether a knot diagram can be coloured with three colours so that every colour is used and each crossing is all-same or all-different

chinese_translations.english: the property of a knot being colourable with three colours under the colouring rules
chinese_translations.example: Tricolourability is a knot invariant: no Reidemeister move can take it away.

english_explanations: able to be coloured with three colours so that each crossing shows three different colours or one single colour

chinese_translations.english: (of a knot diagram) colourable with three colours so that every crossing is all-same or all-different
chinese_translations.example: The trefoil knot is tricolourable, but the figure of eight knot and the unknot are not.

english_explanations: the generalisation of tricolourability from three colours to any prime number of colours

chinese_translations.english: colourability by any prime number p of colours, generalising the rule a + b ≡ 2c (mod 3)
chinese_translations.example: Instead of three colours, prime-colourability allows any prime number of colours.

english_explanations: a property of a knot that does not change under ambient isotopy or any allowed moves

chinese_translations.english: a property that stays the same no matter how the knot is deformed
chinese_translations.example: If one knot has an invariant that the other lacks, the two knots are distinct.

english_explanations: something, such as a number or a polynomial, that does not change under a given set of transformations

chinese_translations.english: a quantity or property that remains the same under allowed transformations
chinese_translations.example: The Alexander polynomial is the most powerful invariant in the article.

english_explanations: a number computed from a knot diagram; a knot is p-colourable exactly when p divides this determinant

chinese_translations.english: a number computed from the knot matrix that determines the prime colourability of a knot
chinese_translations.example: The knot determinant of the trefoil is -3, which is divisible by 3, so the trefoil is tricolourable.

english_explanations: a polynomial invariant of a knot, built from a labelled knot matrix, that generalises the knot determinant

chinese_translations.english: a polynomial that labels every knot uniquely, generalising the knot determinant
chinese_translations.example: Setting t = -1 in the Alexander polynomial -t^2 + t - 1 gives the knot determinant of the trefoil.

english_explanations: a polynomial associated with a knot that helps distinguish knots from one another

chinese_translations.english: a polynomial invariant used to tell knots apart
chinese_translations.example: It is still an open problem whether a knot polynomial can distinguish every knot from all others.

english_explanations: an arbitrary choice of the direction of travel around the knot, denoted by arrows

chinese_translations.english: an arbitrarily chosen direction of travel around the knot, shown by arrows
chinese_translations.example: Choose an orientation for the knot before building the Alexander polynomial.

english_explanations: the knot obtained by reflecting a given knot, which may or may not be equivalent to it

chinese_translations.english: the reflected version of a knot, which may be a different knot altogether
chinese_translations.example: The system works for most knots, mirror images and complicated variations aside.
